title: Tokens and Text Preparation · Level 2
slo: Prepare text for analysis by using tokenization and common preprocessing methods.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe lemmatization? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Lemmatization uses linguistic rules to reduce a word to its base form. Those rules help ensure the result is valid.
Lemmatization uses vocabulary as well as linguistic rules. This supports valid dictionary forms.
Simply chopping endings describes stemming. Lemmatization uses rules and vocabulary instead.

feedback.intrinsic: You could produce a form that is not a valid word.
feedback.instructional: Lemmatization aims for a valid dictionary form, not merely an ending-stripped form.

options.rationale: Labeling nouns and verbs is POS tagging. Lemmatization reduces words to valid base forms.
options.better_fit: This fits when describing POS tagging.

feedback.intrinsic: You would classify grammar instead of finding the required base form.
feedback.instructional: POS tagging assigns grammatical categories; lemmatization returns a lemma.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Lemmatization uses linguistic rules and vocabulary to produce valid dictionary base forms.

exercises.question_text: Removing stop words can help identify important content words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Common readability words can continue to hide the terms that carry the main topics.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Words such as “the,” “a,” and “it” often add little semantic meaning, so excluding them can highlight content words.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Removing common low-meaning words can make important terms easier to identify.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition no longer clearly identifies what an n-gram groups.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the term, then link it to “a sequence” and finish with what the sequence contains.

exercises.correct_answer: An n-gram is a sequence of terms
exercises.explanation: The definition links the name n-gram to its core idea: a sequence of terms treated together.

exercises.question_text: Breaking a body of text into tokens is called ___.

parts.text: Breaking a body of text into tokens is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The chosen method would not perform the initial split into units.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Normalization standardizes surface form, n-gram extraction groups sequences, and POS tagging adds grammar labels. Tokenization is the splitting step.

exercises.explanation: Tokenization creates the individual units that can then be counted or prepared in other ways.

exercises.question_text: A customer-message analyst wants phrase meanings to remain clear during analysis. Which phrases should the analyst treat as n-grams? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is a multi-term phrase that can be treated as one group. Grouping it can preserve meaning that separate words may miss.
This three-term phrase is a trigram. Treating it as a group can preserve its phrase meaning.

options.error_type: Confuses a stop word with a multi-term phrase
options.rationale: “The” is a common stop word and contains only one word. It does not illustrate a multi-term phrase needing grouping.
options.better_fit: This fits when identifying a common word that may be excluded.

feedback.intrinsic: You would group a common readability word instead of a meaningful phrase.
feedback.instructional: Use n-grams for multi-term sequences; “the” is commonly treated as a stop word.

options.rationale: “Running” becoming “run” describes lemmatization. It is not a phrase selected because its terms form one meaning group.
options.better_fit: This fits when showing a valid dictionary base-form conversion.

feedback.intrinsic: You would confuse word-form reduction with phrase grouping.
feedback.instructional: Lemmatization reduces a word to a lemma; n-grams group terms that appear together.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Grouping these phrases can retain meaning that individual words may not show.

exercises.question_text: A support analyst receives thousands of customer support tickets and must count the terms used in them. What should the analyst do first?

options.rationale: Counting terms requires identifiable token units. Tokenization breaks the collection into those units first.
Two-word phrases are bigrams, which are grouped sequences of terms. The terms must first be available as tokens.
options.better_fit: This fits when preserving the meaning of a two-term phrase is the goal.

feedback.intrinsic: Term counting would begin with only selected phrase groups instead of the basic units.
feedback.instructional: Start by tokenizing; use n-grams later when grouped phrases matter.

options.error_type: Confuses tokenization with stop word removal
options.rationale: Stop word removal excludes common low-meaning words. It is not the step that breaks content into countable units.
options.better_fit: This fits when important content words need to stand out.

feedback.intrinsic: You could discard words before first creating the units needed for counting.
feedback.instructional: Tokenization creates tokens; stop word removal is a later choice for focusing on content words.

options.rationale: POS tagging assigns categories such as noun or verb using context. Grammar labels are not needed to create countable tokens.
options.better_fit: This fits when grammatical categories are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: You would spend effort adding grammar labels instead of preparing countable units.
feedback.instructional: Tokenization comes first because it breaks the collection into tokens.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Tokenization provides the units whose frequencies can be counted.

exercises.question_text: Changing all words to lowercase before token generation is text ___.

parts.text: Changing all words to lowercase before token generation is text

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected method would change which words are included or how their forms are reduced instead of standardizing case.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Stop word removal excludes common words, stemming strips endings, and lemmatization finds valid base forms. Lowercasing is normalization.

exercises.explanation: Lowercasing standardizes a surface difference while leaving the word content available for frequency analysis.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The process and the kind of information it assigns are no longer connected clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with POS tagging, then show that it labels each token with a grammatical category.

exercises.correct_answer: POS tagging labels each token with a grammatical category
exercises.explanation: POS tagging acts on each token and assigns a grammatical category such as noun, verb, adjective, or adverb.

exercises.question_text: A customer-feedback analyst is counting terms and does not need capitalization or punctuation details. Which preparation actions should the analyst choose? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Lowercasing standardizes case when capitalization details are not needed. It supports frequency-based counting.
Removing punctuation is suitable when its meaning is not needed. It standardizes content for frequency-based analysis.
A period can carry sentence-ending information, but that detail is not needed here. The stated goal is term counting without punctuation details.
options.better_fit: This fits when sentence-ending punctuation must remain meaningful.

feedback.intrinsic: You would keep a detail the analyst has said is unnecessary for counting terms.
feedback.instructional: Preserve punctuation when it matters; otherwise normalization can remove it for frequency-based analysis.

options.rationale: Valid dictionary base forms require lemmatization. The stated need is only to standardize capitalization and punctuation.
options.better_fit: This fits when words such as “running” must become the valid form “run.”

feedback.intrinsic: You would add base-form processing that does not address the stated surface differences.
feedback.instructional: Lemmatization uses linguistic rules and vocabulary; lowercase and punctuation changes are normalization.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These choices standardize the details that the analyst does not need.

exercises.question_text: Words such as “the,” “a,” and “it” are often called ___.

parts.text: Words such as “the,” “a,” and “it” are often called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The label would confuse common low-meaning words with units, phrases, or dictionary base forms.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Tokens are units, n-grams are term sequences, and lemmas are valid base forms. “The,” “a,” and “it” are stop words.

exercises.explanation: These common readability words often add little semantic meaning, so they may be excluded to highlight content words.

exercises.question_text: A text analyst needs “running” to become the valid dictionary word “run” before analyzing customer feedback. Which method should the analyst use?

options.rationale: Lemmatization uses linguistic rules and vocabulary to return valid dictionary base forms. “Running” to “run” is its stated behavior.

options.error_type: Confuses valid lemma with stripped stem
options.rationale: Stemming strips endings to group related forms. Its result may not be a valid word.
options.better_fit: This fits when consolidating related forms without needing a guaranteed valid dictionary result.

feedback.intrinsic: The analyst may not receive the required valid dictionary word.
feedback.instructional: Choose lemmatization when the result must be a valid lemma such as “run.”

options.rationale: Normalization standardizes punctuation or capitalization. It does not use vocabulary and rules to return “run.”
options.better_fit: This fits when case or punctuation should be standardized before token generation.

feedback.intrinsic: “Running” could remain unchanged as a word form.
feedback.instructional: Normalization handles surface differences; lemmatization reduces a word to a valid base form.

options.error_type: Confuses base-form reduction with phrase grouping
options.rationale: N-gram extraction groups sequences of terms. It does not change a word to its dictionary base form.
options.better_fit: This fits when a multi-term phrase should be treated as a group.

feedback.intrinsic: The needed base form would not be produced.
feedback.instructional: Use lemmatization for valid base forms and n-grams for grouped term sequences.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Lemmatization returns the valid dictionary base form required here.

exercises.question_text: An employee-feedback analyst needs the main topics in comments. Which step should the analyst use to make content words easier to identify?

options.rationale: Removing common low-meaning words can make content words easier to identify. That directly supports finding main topics.

options.error_type: Confuses stop word removal with normalization
options.rationale: Lowercasing standardizes case for frequency-based analysis. It does not remove common readability words.
options.better_fit: This fits when capitalization differences should not affect term counts.

feedback.intrinsic: Common words could still obscure the main topics.
feedback.instructional: Use stop word removal to exclude low-meaning words; use lowercasing to standardize case.

options.error_type: Confuses stop word removal with n-gram extraction
options.rationale: Bigrams preserve the meaning of two-term sequences. They do not remove common words that can hide content terms.
options.better_fit: This fits when a two-word phrase should be treated as a group.

feedback.intrinsic: Frequent common words may remain mixed with the important terms.
feedback.instructional: N-grams group sequences; stop word removal makes content words easier to identify.

options.rationale: Counting occurrences is frequency analysis after tokens are prepared. It does not itself exclude low-meaning words.
options.better_fit: This fits when measuring how often each normalized token appears.

feedback.intrinsic: The count could remain dominated by common readability words.
feedback.instructional: Remove stop words first when the goal is to make important content words stand out.

exercises.explanation: Correct. This removes common words that often add little semantic meaning.
